Equate new items and respondents to a fitted model

Source: R/27_equate.R
equate.Rd

Places a new test form on the scale of a fitted model through the items the two share (the anchor items). The parameters of the fit are held fixed; the new respondents are assigned to its latent classes or ranks, and the items the fit has not seen are placed on the same scale. For the biclustering family (Biclustering(), Ranklustering, and the reference objects of as_biclustering()) a new item is assigned to one of the existing fields, with a diagnostic that tells when none of them fits. For LCA() and LRA() (binary, nominal and ordinal) the reference profile of each new item is estimated, under the order restriction of the fit when the fit is isotonic, or with its filter when the fit is a GTM.

The two unknowns, the membership of the respondents and the parameters of the new items, are updated alternately until the membership settles. The first step uses the anchor items alone, so the scale is the fit's from the start. Anchor items missing from newdata are simply left out; at least one anchor item is required.

Usage

equate(fit, newdata, ...)

# S3 method for class 'exametrika'
equate(
  fit,
  newdata,
  na = NULL,
  maxiter = 100,
  tol = 1e-06,
  alpha = 1,
  M = 10000,
  seed = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted model: LCA() (binary, nominal), LRA() (binary, ordinal), Biclustering() (binary, nominal, ordinal, rated) or a reference object from as_biclustering(). The rated LCA and LRA, the SOM, the IRM and the network models are not supported.

newdata

New responses: a matrix or data frame with the items in columns, or an exametrikaData object from dataFormat(). Column names are required: the items whose names match the fit are the anchor items, every other column is a new item. Missing responses (NA, or the codes given in na) are left out of the likelihood. Responses must use the coding of the fitted data.

...

Not used.

na

Values to treat as missing, besides NA.

maxiter

Maximum number of alternating cycles.

tol

The cycles stop when no membership probability moves by more than this.

alpha

Concentration of the Beta or Dirichlet prior of the new-field diagnostic (biclustering) and of the reference profiles of the new items (nominal and ordinal one-mode models). Default 1, the flat prior of the estimation.

M

Number of particles of the Monte Carlo behind the order restriction in the diagnostic of an isotonic fit; see ICL_exact.

seed

Seed of that Monte Carlo (the global stream is left untouched).

Value

An object of class exametrikaEquate, a list with

Membership, Estimate, log_lik

As in predict.exametrika(): the posterior membership of the new respondents, their class or rank, and the log-likelihood of each respondent under the model.

AnchorItems, NewItems

The item labels of the two groups.

FieldMembership, FieldEstimated

Biclustering: the posterior field membership of each new item and the field with the largest probability.

NewFieldLogBF

Biclustering: the log Bayes factor of "a field of its own" against "one of the existing fields" for each new item (see Details). NA when the Monte Carlo could not resolve the order probability; the value reported is then a bound, with a warning.

AnchorLogBF

Biclustering: the same quantity for the anchor items of newdata, the yardstick for the new items. With many respondents every item departs measurably from its field profile, so a new item stands out only when it scores well above the anchor items.

NewItems

Biclustering: the three columns above as a data frame.

IRP

Binary LCA / LRA: the item reference profile of each new item (items x classes).

ICRP

Nominal LCA / ordinal LRA: the category reference profile of each new item, one row per category, in the layout of the fit.

n_cycle, converge, total_log_lik

Cycles run, whether tol was met, and the sum of log_lik.

Details

For a biclustering fit the field reference profiles are never changed, so a new item can only be placed in a field the fit already has. To tell whether that is appropriate, NewFieldLogBF compares, for each new item, the marginal likelihood of its responses under a field of its own (the block probabilities integrated out under the prior of the fit, as in ICL_exact; the Beta or Dirichlet with parameter alpha, restricted to the ordered region when the fit is isotonic) with the marginal likelihood under the existing fields (equal prior weight on each field). The respondents enter with their hard assignment, as in ICL_exact. A positive value says that the item behaves unlike every field of the fit; in that case the field it was given is the least bad one, and a new field should be considered when the fit is revised. Because a field profile is an average over its items, a single item departs from it more and more measurably as the respondents grow in number, and even the fitted items come out positive in a large sample. The same quantity is therefore computed for the anchor items of newdata (AnchorLogBF), and a new item is read against that range rather than against zero.

Examples

# \donttest{
# A new form: ten items of the fitted test as anchors, two new items
fit <- Biclustering(J15S500, ncls = 3, nfld = 2, method = "B", verbose = FALSE)
X <- J15S500$U[1:100, ]
colnames(X)[11:12] <- c("new1", "new2")
eq <- equate(fit, X[, 1:12])
eq$NewItems
#>   ItemLabel Field Membership     logBF
#> 1      new1     2          1 -3.809214
#> 2      new2     2          1 -0.621552
head(eq$Estimate)
#> Student1 Student2 Student3 Student4 Student5 Student6 
#>        1        2        2        3        1        3 
# }
